Did you hear that, General Blaskic? The question was to know whether it was a regular thing, was it an ordinary thing to be promoted to a high position in another army when one was in your situation as the head of the army of the federation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: My chief was the president of the presidency and president of the federation, Kresimir Zubak. I know that there was an agreement on cooperation, that is, military cooperation between Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia. I don't know what arrangements were made here because I did not take part in that and I do not know of those arrangements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let me ask you this question: Do you know of any other army in the world where a president of one country can give orders to an army of another country?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It depends on the military agreements. I don't know how NATO works, its military alliance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that the witness has answered. It depends on whether there were cooperative arrangements and agreements. Judge Rodrigues?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Kehoe. General Blaskic, I'd like to ask you the following question: If I've understood you correctly, the HVO officers were appointed to the Croatian army as part of a cooperative agreement; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I said that a military agreement between the Republic of Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, which for awhile was called the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was in existence. I know that there was some training, some equipping. There was a later split agreement and split declaration. There were joint operations for the liberation of certain areas in which both the Croatian army and the Bosnian army participated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Therefore, the appointments of officers in the HVO was not done as part of that cooperative agreement or were they, in fact, part of that cooperative agreement?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, I never had this document in my hands on the military agreements in order to be able to fully answer your question, but I know that President Zubak relieved me of my duty with the HVO. My duty in the HVO ceased based on an order of the commander in chief, Kresimir Zubak. I don't know whether this was due to the indictment that was issued against me or whether it was some other issue which had to do with the Washington Accords.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I have two other questions. You said that as part of those agreements, those cooperative agreements, between Croatia and the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there were officers from the federation who were participants in several exchanges; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm afraid the question I received was not received. Your question was whether there were officers involved in the exchanges?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: If I understood you correctly, General Blaskic, you said that there was a cooperative agreement between Croatia and the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and within that cooperation, there was training, military training, et cetera. I'm not sure if I understood what you said correctly.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know of an agreement between the Republic of Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina on cooperation, and within the framework of this cooperation, I don't know how it was organised, but I know that it was a train-and-equip programme and then troops being sent to the front lines and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: In that cooperation, did only the officers of the HVO participate or were there also participants by the officers of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I would say that there were participants on the part of the officer corps and soldiers of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina but it was in various locations and at various levels. Let me just point out that I'm aware of three brigades who were trained and equipped in Croatia and sent to Central Bosnia to fight against the army of Republika Srpska alongside the HVO, and those were brigades of the BH army. I'm also aware of the assistance which was sent to Bihac in cooperation with the BH army officers in the Bihac area for the defence of the Bihac pocket. I'm also aware of the assistance in the Posavina region, in the north of Bosnia, which was in cooperation with the 2nd BH Army Corps in Croatia, but I do not know the exact details of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Here's the other question I'd like to ask you: There were HVO officers like yourself who were promoted in the Croatian army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were HVO officers who, on the basis of their requests, joined, that is, continued their service in the HV because their duties in the HVO ceased on various grounds. Whether the duty was no more or they were not needed any longer, there were such cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: I have another question, perhaps a little naive, but I'd like to ask it anyway. Were there officers of the BH army who were promoted within that same framework? Do you know whether there were any officers of the BH army who were promoted also in the Croatian army, the HV?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the 2nd Army Corps, I'm not sure, but I think that somebody from the 2nd BH Army Corps was. I know that there were officers in the BH army who, when the federation army was created, did transfer from the BH army to the HVO. It is possible that today there were some who, from the army, did transfer to the HV, but I do not have such specific information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Rodrigues. I know that you haven't finished asking your question, but if you agree, we can stop now, and we will resume at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.04 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We can resume the hearing now. Please be seated. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Just a point of order before the questioning commences. Mr. President and Your Honours, if we could ask for approximately 10 minutes at the end of the day for an ex parte in camera matter concerning a recent incident that has come to the attention -- not having to do with this, but if we can take that period of time towards the end of the day, the Office of the Prosecutor would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me turn to my colleagues. We're always not comfortable when we ask for ex parte hearings when we don't know what it is about. Since you can't do it because you need to have ex parte in order to explain why you need ex parte. Well, we have enough trust in Defence counsel and in the Prosecution counsel, so after we have had the Defence agreement -- I assume there is no comment that either of you wishes to make; is that correct? Mr. Nobilo, you look a bit perplexed. Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We don't know what it's about, so we don't know what comments to make, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. You are exactly in the same situation as the Judges, Mr. Hayman. All right. What I suggest -- well, let me first consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, we trust the court to exercise its proper discretion. If an ex parte contact on whatever it is is not appropriate we, of course, put that matter in the court's hands. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Judges have confidence in you, Mr. Kehoe, and for that reason we'll have the ex parte but that means we'll stop at quarter after five. Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. On that issue, I believe Mr. Harmon will address the court, not me, on the issue of the ex parte in camera matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to take advantage of this occasion to say to you Mr. Kehoe, and ask you and ask the witness as well to try to demonstrate a spirit of synthesis both in the questions and in the answers. You know that very frequently the Trial Chamber makes efforts in order to synthesise things. Instead of asking for a motion, we don't always have to say we're going to suspend the hearing, we're going to interrupt things, but we try to settle things as quickly as possible. Therefore, try to make an effort. Having said this, Mr. Kehoe, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, just one follow-up question to the question that was asked by Judge Rodrigues. General, do you know of any Bosnian Muslim officer from the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina who was appointed and ordered to become a part of the HV by President Tudjman? Do you know any such officer, and if so, the name, please?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, the only thing I said was that I had information that there were transfers of the BH army officers to the HVO and HV. At this point in time, I do not know what their ethnic background was, whether they were Serbs, Muslims, Gypsies, whatever their religion was, but I know they were members of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let us move ahead and we will talk about the period of time when you came back from Austria to become a part and a member of the HVO. Now, you noted during your direct-examination that you arrived in Zagreb on the 5th of April, 1992, and my question for you is: When you got to Zagreb on the 5th of April, 1992, did you speak to anybody in the government of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Prior to leaving for Kiseljak, did you speak to anybody in the government of the Republic of Croatia? I'm referring to the time frame when you were still in Austria.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I recollect, no, I did not. You're talking about the period when I have left the JNA and was in Austria?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not talk to the officials there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you did speak to Bosnian Croat officials who were in Bosnia during this time frame, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I talked to the officials in the Kiseljak municipality. He was a Bosnian Croat from Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: His name was Pero Madzar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you discuss the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, absolutely nothing in that regard. Those were short conversations where he conveyed to me the position of the president of the municipality assembly and conveyed his request that I come and provide him with my expertise and assistance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had no discussions whatsoever about the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, what it was about, what it stood for, what its plans were for the future; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. At that time when I was in Austria, the only conversation I had was to the effect of my coming to help the defence of Kiseljak municipality against the potential aggressor which was the army of the Republika Srpska, actually at that time still the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now you left Zagreb for Kiseljak on the 6th of April, and when did you think you were going to get to Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believed that I would arrive in the course of the day of the 6th of April, sometime in the evening, that I would reach Kiseljak, but I did not have full understanding of what the passibility of the roads was at that time. That was the beginning of the conflict, so travel on those roads was actually fairly uncertain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, this was the 6th. It was one day before the Republic of Croatia recognised the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and offered dual citizenship within the Croatian nation, and two days before the formation of the HVO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said when I had planned on getting there. If you say so, it is possible that it is so, but I know, on the 8th of April the HVO was established. So that was two days prior. I'm not sure about the exact date when both the Republic of Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina were recognised. It could be the day that you refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'll move through this quickly, Mr. President, as opposed to going through all of these documents seriatim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I can only agree with that intent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Prosecutor's Exhibit 406/5 is the recognition by the Republic of Croatia, by Dr. Franjo Tudjman, dated the 7th of April, 1992. Prosecutor's Exhibit 38, tab 21, page 4, is as the witness just reflected, the formation of the Croatian Defence Council, or HVO, on the 8th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If it isn't being contested, because it depends upon you -- do you want to have the witness confirm that it was the 7th of April or do you have any other questions you want to ask about that same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's quite all right, Mr. President. The document speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think it's simply a date that has to be recognised. It's in the case file, I believe, already. Is that not true, Mr. Registrar, or is it something new?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As regards 406/5, yes, that exhibit is in the case file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's not indispensable. I don't believe that the witness contests the date. Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question was improperly put to the witness. Three questions were merged into one. There was one question that was slipped into this question, which was that on the same date that President Tudjman had offered dual citizenship to the Bosnian Croats. We would like to see that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can put it on the ELMO. We can show the witness 406/5. That's fine. I figured we'd do this more quickly, but if we have to do it the slow way around, please. We could give that exhibit to the witness. (Technical difficulty)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Is it working now? Do you hear? Is it all right now? Does everybody hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't know if you were telling me to do something because I didn't get the translation of your last comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I simply noted that Mr. Nobilo preferred that the document be produced; therefore, we're going to produce it. That was what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, because the witness testified nothing about the dual citizenship issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We're going to look at the document. Let's move forward. As long as we can, let's do so. We will go forward as quick as we can. If we have to take a step backward when we have to, then we will. Mr. Kehoe, please proceed. General Blaskic, you've read the document; I suppose you're familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had not seen this document before, Your Honours. I did review it just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, the recognition of the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the Republic of Croatia, number 2 says: "This act of recognition grants the right of dual citizenship to the members of the Croatian nation who wish such citizenship." That was the reference point to which I was addressing the Court to prior to this discussion about the documents.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your permission, paragraph 2 has not been read in its entirety, "and we suggest that this issue be agreed to by a bilateral agreement process," which means that, in paragraph 2, they are saying -- just pointing out the guidelines as to how to go about this dual citizenship issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General Blaskic, you were in Zagreb on the 5th, you were in Kiseljak on the 6th -- excuse me, due to leave for Kiseljak on the 6th and due to get in the next day, except for your capture. This particular document, 406/5, is dated the 7th, is that correct, the 7th of April?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, this document is dated 7 April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the HVO was established on the 8th of April, as you noted just previously; correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The HVO was established on the 8th of April, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, was it an organised plan to bring Bosnian Croat officers such as yourself back to Central Bosnia and other areas that were covered by the HVO during this time frame?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know anything about some organised plan, nor did I have any conversation about any organised plans. The only thing I know is that at that time in the Kiseljak municipality, which is my municipality, there were the former JNA officers, both Croat and Bosniak, who were engaged in the defence of the municipality because it borders on the Ilija, Rakovica, and Hadzici municipalities which were already under Serb control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the exact date that you reported to the municipal authorities in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: On 14 April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By the 23rd of April of 1992, you had been appointed the commander of the armed formations of the municipal crisis staff in Kiseljak; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your question came across that I had been appointed by the 23rd of April. Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 23rd of April, were you appointed the head of the armed forces of the municipal crisis staff, 23 April, the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I was appointed by the president of the municipal crisis staff as commander of the armed formations of the Kiseljak municipality together with Bakir Alispahic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, were you in agreement with the political positions of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna that were being expressed in Kiseljak during the time frame when you got there?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: At that time, in April, that is, the municipal crisis staff was active in Kiseljak. It was composed of representatives of Croats and Muslims, and this staff was appointed by the Kiseljak municipality assembly, so it was not appointed by the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna but the Kiseljak municipality assembly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, with regard to the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, were you in agreement with the political policies of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna when you arrived in Kiseljak and by the time you were appointed on the 23rd of April, 1992? Were you in agreement with those policies?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I perceived the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna as an organisation of the self-organised -- as a community of self-organised Croatian people against the aggression of the Serbs. At that time, I had not enough basis to form any political opinion, nor was I particularly interested in that. My preoccupation in Kiseljak was of a military nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us discuss some paragraphs in Prosecutor's Exhibit 406/2, a document dated the 12th of November, 1991, sometime before you got to Kiseljak but, nonetheless, being drafted by Mate Boban and Dario Kordic. Let us put that on the ELMO, and this is the minutes or conclusions of a joint meeting of the Herzegovina Regional Community and the Travnik Regional Community. The president of the regional crisis staff for Herzegovina is Mate Boban, and the president of the Travnik Regional Community is Dario Kordic. Let's go to the conclusions, and I will read this slowly: "1. The Croatian Regional Community and the Travnik Regional Community remain of the opinion stated in the conclusions adopted at earlier meetings, that the Croatian people of this region, and of all Bosnia and Herzegovina, still support the unanimously accepted orientation and conclusions adopted in agreements with president Dr. Franjo Tudjman on 13 and 20 June, 1991 in Zagreb. On basis of the conclusions of the above-mentioned meetings and agreement in Zagreb, as well as the separate conclusions of 15 October, 1991 in Grude, and 22 October, 1991 in Busovaca, and on this occasion, 12 November, 1991, these two regional communities have unanimously decided that the Croatian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina must finally embrace a determined and active policy which will realise our eternal dream - a common Croatian State. "In order that historic goal may soon also be our reality, these two regional communities ask that legal and political documents be prepared and published (proclaiming a Croatian Banovina in BH and the holding of a referendum on joining the Republic of Croatia) as the first steps on the road to the final solution of the Croatian question and the creation of" and then "words illegible." Let us move down to 3(a) of this document which notes that: "3. In order to implement the conclusions from the first two items of these conclusions, we must: a) clearly define the party politics of the HDZ and BH, strengthen its membership, and select people who can see these tasks through to end." Now, General, were you one of those people who was selected by officials such as Kordic and Boban to see their tasks to the end, that is, the fulfilment of their eternal dream, a common Croatian state? Were you one of those people?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, vague as to "officials such as Kordic and Boban." Why doesn't counsel ask the witness if he ever met Mr. Kordic, if he ever met Mr. Boban, if he had any contact. Was he invited by any of the people listed in this document to come to Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, we already have in the record numerous pictures of the two of them together --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I would like the Prosecutor to be able to ask his questions properly. Mr. Kehoe, ask your questions. You see, the question has not even been asked and then there's an objection. The Prosecutor can ask whether the witness -- the witness wants to answer the way he wants to answer. That's all. Simply try to ask your question more clearly. Ask your question again and then let's hear the answer, but objections are being made before answers are given. The Judges realise what this means because when one makes an objection, Mr. Hayman, that requires an answer from the witness. You understand what I mean? I don't think that you did that on purpose. I know you didn't do that on purpose, but that can be interpreted that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: My training, Mr. President, is to object to an objectionable question because the witness shouldn't have to answer an objectionable question. That was my purpose. I apologise if the Court is offended by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: My training, Mr. Hayman, my training is to direct the proceedings so that they are carried out equitably. Mr. Kehoe, ask your question as you want to ask it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, given the goal of bringing the Croatian people together as part of the Republic of Croatia, were you one of those people that was brought in and ordered to see that task to the end?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Let me first answer like this: I do not feel that that is what it was and, Your Honours, I had never seen this document before. This document was not signed. I did not talk to the creators, the drafters of this document, and I never attended this meeting. There are several meetings quoted here. I never attended any one of those. If I can only be given a moment to review these two conclusions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. You've got the right to review the document, and I pointed out to your counsel that you have the right to answer as you wish. All right, look at the document. How much time do you need in order to look at it, a minute, two minutes?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Maybe a couple of minutes so I can see what it is about, because as I said, I did not attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Take two or three minutes. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, now that you've familiarised yourself with that document which you never saw before; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I familiarised myself with the document, and I have already stated to the Trial Chamber what my motivation for coming to Central Bosnia were. That was my expertise and assistance in preparation for the defence of my municipality together with all other citizens of the municipality. I consider this document to be a political one. I never discussed it with the authors on any of these issues.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, prior to you coming to Kiseljak, were you told that officials in Central Bosnia were having contact with the Republic of Croatia, seeking their advice and/or support during that time frame, before you got to Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was only told to provide assistance, even on a temporary basis, to my municipality in preparations for the defence. That was my expert military assistance. In other words, I was asked to provide my expert military assistance on the basis of my military training. I was never offered any other contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us look at Prosecutor's Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Judge Rodrigues?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: General Blaskic, I believe that the contacts that occurred with you when you were in Austria, I believe that those contacts were made by the President of the municipality of Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, his duty was that of the president of the Kiseljak municipality assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. Here's my question: How did these contacts come about?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know whether -- are you referring to the -- you mean technically how they were conducted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to leave you with the answer. When I say "how," I meant was it by telephone, was it by mail, was it by video-conference, was it by -- in some way? How did you communicate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Now you've made it clear for me. We communicated on the telephone, this is Mr. Pero Madzar, and he conveyed to me these requests on the part of the president of the Kiseljak municipality assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Do you remember about how frequently this contact occurred? Was it one contact or were there several contacts?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were several contacts. If it is important I can look in my chronology, but it was more than one contact. There were multiple contacts. I remember that we talked -- that we had one contact every 7 or maybe every 15 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand now. Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Rodrigues. Please continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in this document, the writers, Mate Boban, who subsequently became the Commander in Chief of the HVO, and Dario Kordic, who was one of the vice-presidents of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, note that this, "Joining of the Croatian people in a common Croatian state is an eternal dream and a historic goal." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that in the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can show the witness Defence Exhibit 300. I apologise. This was not on the list but it is one we discussed this morning. Now, Exhibit 300, General, is your attack order to the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade on Kiseljak, on the 17th of April, 1993, at 23.45, where you instruct the attack to commence the next morning at 5.30. In paragraph 9 of that document you tell that brigade to, "Maintain a sense of historic responsibility." Now, General, this eternal dream, and this historic goal, and your reference to "historic responsibility" are all referring to the same thing, aren't they? Carving out a common Croatian state, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. That is absolutely not so. On the 17th of April, I was on the brink of total collapse and the loss of all positions in the Lasva pocket. Unfortunately, I was forced to take steps to relieve the burden on the front line in the Lasva pocket. Being in such a situation, it was quite normal that as the commander, I should encourage my subordinates to carry out that task. My fundamental position was to relieve the pressure on the Lasva pocket, which was about to fall. If the Ban Josip Jelacic Brigade had not reacted, I'm confident that we would have lost the Lasva pocket. So this was meant to encourage the combat morale of the soldiers and the command. It is something that any commander would do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This eternal dream and this goal and historic responsibility have nothing to do with each other; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not talking about goals here. I don't know what your question is, but point 9 is quite clear, "Bear in mind your responsibilities," that is, the responsibility for the combat assignment given. According to the standards of the former JNA, one of the points for the security of combat operations was the security of morale, so that the military assignments would be carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to the Republic of Croatia, did you know that officials in Central Bosnia were meeting with the Republic of Croatia before you got to Kiseljak on the 14th of April?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That the offices -- could you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that officials in Central Bosnia, including Dario Kordic, were meeting with officials of the Republic of Croatia, including Gojko Susak, the Defence Minister? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. I never knew the president of the municipality of Kiseljak before that date. Physically we never met. I left to attend school, when I was 15, in Zagreb, and I spent most of these years in military training. As a military man of the former JNA, I lived in a completely autonomous system, without any need to communicate with my original municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, what year did you mention? Could you be more specific about the year?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The document is what? Please be very precise, because the document that you showed the witness was the 17th of April, 1993. So there is a time gap that we have to be aware of. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move to Prosecutor's Exhibit 406/4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, perhaps before going forward, General Blaskic, I should like to go back to my previous question. The President of the municipal assembly of Kiseljak called you once, twice, three times. It's irrelevant, but several times. Do you remember well the words used, how he spoke to you? Could you now perhaps make a summary of that conversation, how he invited you to come? What did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, I never said in my testimony that I was called by the President of the municipal assembly of Kiseljak. It wasn't he who called me. I was contacted by Mr. Pero Madzar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, General. I apologise. But anyway, the person who spoke in the name of the president and who contacted you, what expressions did he use in speaking to you? Do you understand my question? Yes, I take into account your correction.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, I again got a different interpretation. "The person who had contacted you, holding the position of president of the municipality." I must repeat, it was not the President of the municipality who contacted me by phone while I was in Austria. Maybe something's wrong with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. My question is: The person who contacted you, and according to you, on behalf of the president of the municipal assembly. Is that okay now, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: (No translation)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: How did that conversation go?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Pero Madzar said to me that he had contacted me on the authority of the president of the assembly of the municipality of Kiseljak, and that he was asking me to come back to the municipality of Kiseljak to provide professional assistance in preparing and organising the defence of the municipality of Kiseljak. That was the substance of that conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Did he speak to you about reasons or motives, why they were calling you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. He said that in the territory of Kiseljak municipality they lacked professional military men and that they would welcome my professional military assistance. I told him later on that I would agree to come only temporarily, and he conveyed that position further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Another question, General. In relation to the President of the municipal assembly, you said that you had never met him personally, because you left to study, et cetera. Mr. Pero Madzar, did you have any personal contact with him before? Did you know him from before or not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was my neighbour living some 700 metres away from me. After I had left to study, that is, in 1975, I may have come across him but we never had any particular contacts after that. He's four years my senior, so that even before we didn't have much contact, but I know him well, I know where his house is, and very rarely did I have contacts with officials of the Kiseljak municipality while I was serving in the Republic of Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: My last question for the moment: Did you know how he was able to get in touch with you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He asked my parents to give him my telephone number, and my late father gave him my telephone number and that is how he called me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If we could move to 406/4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a document that's in evidence, dated the 21st of March, 1992, concerning a meeting with the Minister of Defence. The request is to the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia and reads as follows: "At the meeting of the commanders of Central Bosnia held on 17 March, 1992 in Busovaca, a meeting with the Minister of Defence of the Republic of Croatia, Mr. Gojko Susak, was considered imperative. We would like to request a meeting with you in order to inform you about the current situation in Central Bosnia and the problems we encounter and to receive your instructions for further actions in this area. The following representatives would attend the meeting: Mr. Pasko Ljubicic, commander of the Central Bosnia command; Mr. Zvonko Vukovic, head of the Central Bosnia command; Mr. Dario Kordic, head of the Crisis Committee for Central Bosnia, Vice-President of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; and Mr. Boris," the name is illegible, "President of the Executive Board of the Travnik municipal assembly. We would be very grateful if you would meet with us and, if possible, schedule the meeting for next week." Signed by Pasko Ljubicic. Now, Pasko Ljubicic, General, is the individual that you met on the 5th of May, 1992 as the commander of the Central Bosnia command; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I met him. Could you repeat the date? I didn't quite get the date because I was reading the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date you told us that you met Pasko Ljubicic was the 5th of May, 1992. That's what you testified to on the record?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Pasko Ljubicic is the man I met on that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know Zvonko Vukovic? He was the initial commander of the 4th Military Police Battalion, and then he was also the commander of the home guards in Central Bosnia. You know that gentleman, do you not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I know him. I know Zvonko Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, you know Dario Kordic?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know him too. I met him at the same time as Pasko Ljubicic. I think it was in May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, did this meeting take place with Gojko Susak and did these gentlemen tell you about this meeting with Gojko Susak?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, my answer to this question is that I do not know whether this meeting took place and, secondly, at the time this document was drafted, I was in Austria. I did not attend the meeting on the 17th of March, 1992 in Busovaca. I did not speak to the author of this document, Pasko Ljubicic, about this document, and I know nothing about these events or this document, including whether the meeting was held or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not troops of the HV for the Republic of Croatia were ordered to Bosnia shortly after this scheduled meeting?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that I don't even know whether this meeting took place. I don't know what the question was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is this: By April of 1992, were there HV troops in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In April '92? When in April? I was still in Austria in April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's start with by the time you got there on the 14th of April, 1992. Were there HV troops in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I came to the Kiseljak municipality, and I can speak about that municipality. I didn't see any Croatian army troops there. Whether there were any such troops elsewhere, I do not know and I cannot provide an answer. I don't know whether at that time there were any Croatian army troops. There weren't any in the municipality of Kiseljak. If you're asking me about the whole of Bosnia and Herzegovina, there may have been some, but I have no information about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, let me read a portion of your testimony, and I'm reading on page 17867. This is you from lines 7 through 23: "At the session of the municipal crisis staff, around the 23rd of April, 1992, I was appointed the commander of the armed formations by the municipal crisis staff in Kiseljak, and I was not, either in the first contact or later, led to believe that there was a military structure superior to the municipality from which I was to seek either approval or which was to verify this appointment of mine. "Also, as far as my work is concerned, I never was aware of any superior structure, something that I could relate to my previous work, in other words, an entity to which I would report my daily activities. I would only occasionally inform members of the municipal crisis staff in Kiseljak on my activities or members of the HVO headquarters in Kiseljak, and there was no superior military structure in existence at the time above this." Do you recall that testimony, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall that testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't true, was it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is true on the 23rd of April, if that is what you're talking about. A military structure had not been established. I reported to the municipal crisis staff and members of the Kiseljak staff, and that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me start with this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could we have the page? It's not on 17867.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, it is. 17867, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Lines 7 to 23?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's right. I have the page here. What can I tell you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I have the page. It's not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's right here.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 578.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could put that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, do you recognise that man?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: General Janko Bobetko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he is wearing a general's uniform from the HV similar to yours; right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I turn to the next exhibit which is 406/6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, was this a general of the Croatian army or of the HVO? I didn't quite get that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The Croatian army, never the HVO -- well, I shouldn't say "never the HVO." It depends what day you're talking about. He has "HV" on his lapels.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Excuse me. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us turn our attention to 406/6, Prosecutor's Exhibit 406/6. That's on the ELMO. This is an order from President Franjo Tudjman, and it says: "Pursuant to Article 52, paragraph 1, item of the Law on Defence, and in view of the extraordinary circumstances in connection with the escalation of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which also threatens the border regions of the Republic of Croatia, I hereby issue the following: "Order: By which I appoint General Janko Bobetko, commander of all units of the Croatian army on the southern front, from Split to Dubrovnik. "In this regard, all commands in that sector including those of the Croatian navy shall be subordinated to him. "A staff of the southern front shall also be formed from their ranks as needed. "This order shall take effect immediately. 10 April, 1992. Signed, President Franjo Tudjman, Republic of Croatia." Now, General Blaskic, the southern front discussed in this particular document encompasses Central Bosnia, the area that you were operating in which ultimately became the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The southern front is here delineated by the region of Split and the region of Dubrovnik; therefore, it doesn't include Central Bosnia. This is the first time I hear of any such statement. According to my military training, Central Bosnia was never part of the southern front. According to the former division of the JNA, when military geography was studied, there was a strategic axis called Split-Vrbas going from Split via Kupres towards Jajce and Banja Luka but never from Split towards Central Bosnia. This is the first I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 406/16, if we could put that on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we're going to go on to another document, we've been working for an hour, so, if possible, could we make a break now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could finish this document, this particular area on this document before we take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I beg the Court's indulgence that we finish this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Finish, yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we take a look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 406/16, this is a document on the Republic of Croatia letterhead, "Southern Front Command, Split Operative Zone Command, Ploce Forward Command Post." The date: "19 May, 1992." This document is dated four days before you meet Zarko Tole; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I met Zarko Tole in Busovaca, but I didn't see this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Formation of the forward command post "Central Bosnia." "With the aim of organising effective defence and integrating the existing Commands in Central Bosnia, I hereby order: 1. Establish forward command post Central Bosnia in Gornji Vakuf. 2. I appoint Brigadier Zarko Tole commander of the forward command post. 3. Brigadier Zarko Tole has all the authorities of coordinating and commanding forces in the Central Bosnia region (Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik, Travnik, Bugojno, Gornji Vakuf, Prozor, Tomislavgrad, and Posusje). 4. Brigadier Zarko Tole shall appoint the necessary number of officers and non-commissioned officers for effective work at the forward command post. 5. This order shall take effect immediately. Commander of the southern front, General Janko Bobetko." This is a document, General, signed by a three-star general in the Croatian army giving command for Central Bosnia to Zarko Tole on the 19th of May, four days before you meet him as the commander of the Central Bosnia command; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct, only he was the commander of the southern front along the Dubrovnik-Split axis, and I said that it covered the Split-Vrbas direction. I can show this to you on the map, the region of Split leading across the Kupres plateaux along the Vrbas River Valley, and the Vrbas River flows through Gornji Vakuf. At that time, I was the commander in the municipal staff of Kiseljak. Kiseljak is not in this order. There is no Kresevo. There is no Fojnica. I don't know what General Bobetko was guided by when he issued this order, and I never discussed this document with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact of the matter, General, is that a general in the Croatian army is both setting up the forward command post for Central Bosnia and appointing Brigadier Zarko Tole as the commander for Central Bosnia four days before you meet Tole.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All I can say is what I see on the document. Whether forward command posts were established or not, I don't know. I wasn't there to check. I was one of the commanders of units in Kiseljak municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, I think that your answer has to be connected to your previous answer. I think that's the point. In your previous answer, you said that the southern front went from Split to Dubrovnik, and you said, in a rather authoritative way, that you don't see how Central Bosnia could be part of this southern front. Now you have a document before you offered by the Prosecutor which, if I understand well, contradicts what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was commenting on the document that I had before me, and that was the order of President Tudjman to the order of the command of the southern front where mention is made of Dubrovnik and Split. I said that, as far as I know, Split includes the Split-Vrbas axis, that is, the Vrbas River Valley towards Banja Luka. That is the military division. At that time, I was in Kiseljak, and Kiseljak is not part of this. The Prosecutor said, "Your area was part of the southern front." At that time, I was in Kiseljak, commander of the municipal staff or, rather, the armed units of the municipal staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I'm not insisting, General. I'm just drawing your attention to your replies to these two documents. Have you any further questions on this document, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Not on this document, Mr. President, but I have others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: On this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No. I have other questions on other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Let's have a 15-minute break because we will be having another break later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let us resume our work. Please be seated. Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, was General Bobetko in the HV or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honours, General Bobetko was in the Croatian army. From this document of May 1992, he was commander of the southern front of the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document that you're talking about is the document that's dated the 19th of May, 1992, which is Prosecutor's Exhibit 406/16. With the assistance of the usher, I'd ask you, General, to take a look at Exhibit 406/10. Again, this is a Prosecutor's exhibit. I apologise without the preliminary description. Now, General, this is a document that's dated approximately a month prior to the order to Zarko Tole on the 19th of May, 1992, again another order or appointment signed by Janko Bobetko, but this document, as you can see -- let's read it. It says, "The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Croatian Defence Council, southern front command. Grude, forward command post. Dated 20 April, 1992. Appointment of officers to the defence command of Tomislavgrad. In order to achieve effective, operational, and secure command in the units of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna the following are appointed: 1. Tole Zarko, Colonel, commander. 2. Siljeg Zeljko, Major, deputy commander. 3. Smiljanic, Jozo, Captain, chief of operations and training section. 4. --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If the witness has the document in front of him, as we all do, perhaps we can wait for a moment for the witness to look at it and then respond. General Blaskic, are you ready? I mean, it doesn't take long to read it. Your question, please, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, General, this document that we're talking about, 406/10, dated the 20th of April, 1992, appointing Zarko Tole, a Colonel, and it's on HVO letterhead, and 406/16, approximately a month later, is another document signed by General Bobetko, appointing now Brigadier Zarko Tole to the Central Bosnia forward command post. I ask you, with these two documents, one where Bobetko is signing on HVO letterhead and the second one on HV letterhead, which army is Bobetko a member of or are they the same army?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: It is not the same army and, Your Honours, allow me please to answer. From this document and from the document that came into being one month later, it is clearly visible that at that time in Bosnia-Herzegovina there was not an organised armed force of the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, neither Muslim Bosniak people in Bosnia-Herzegovina. That I believe the command of the southern front prevented, with this attempt, the downfall of Bosnia-Herzegovina overall into the hands of the army of the Republika Srpska, because had there been a joining up of forces, Serbian forces from eastern Herzegovina via Kupres, Bosnia-Herzegovina would be completely surrounded, whereas this document appoints Mr. Zarko Tole as commander of the command of the defence of Tomislavgrad. The object of this document is quite clear. "In the aim of achieving effective, operational, and secure command," as it says. It doesn't say -- it says ucinkovito, effective, efficacious. In order that one month later the previous order that we looked at today shown to me by the Prosecutor, Colonel Zarko Tole became Brigadier, and I am asking myself whether he had the time to organise this command post while he had become commander of another command post at the same time. What I want to add, Your Honours, that the Central Bosnia mentioned in the previous document does not include the Kiseljak municipality. It does not include Kresevo municipality or Fojnica municipality. It does not include Zepce or the central Operative Zone of Central Bosnia that I'm talking about. Now, why is this? It is because the HVO was not functioning, because the HVO was established in this stage, the stage we're talking about, this point in time. I said that from the previous commander, I received a blue notebook, which was called the wartime diary, two secretaries, but there was no operative command. Never as the command of the Kiseljak municipality did I ever write a report to the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, Brigadier Zarko Tole, because the command did not function. This was a period of time when in Bosnia-Herzegovina the fight was being waged for the survival of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Did that previous order to which you refer and which was signed by General Bobetko, did it specify Vitez and Travnik?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure, Your Honour. I think the best thing would be for us to have a look at it. It is with the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Have a look at it again, yes.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: But at that time I was in Kiseljak. I was a small commander of the armed forces in Kiseljak at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Look at item 3. I have the French before me, and so I will not attempt the impossible, but I do see the names Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik, Travnik.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: But there is no Kiseljak, there is no Kresevo, or Fojnica, or Kakanj, or Vares, or Zepce, or Maglaj, or Usora.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: I grant you that, but do these names suggest that General Bobetko was thinking that Vitez, and Novi Travnik, and Travnik were part of Central Bosnia command?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: This command, the command stipulated in this document here, Your Honour, I suppose that he had that in mind, but I still maintain that it was contrary to the former literature and manuals relating to military geography which we used to prepare examinations for the Major's examination. This central area was never in the Split-Vrebac direction, axis. For me as a soldier, it is very strange to note that he included these towns into that operative and strategic axis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I've now got the English. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, did you get an answer to your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: My question was this, Mr. President, and I did not get an answer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Looking at these two documents, 406/10 dated the 20th of April, 1992, and 406/16 dated 19 May, 1992, my question is: Was General Bobetko, after signing these orders, a General in the HVO, or a General in the HV?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: When he signed these orders, at that time I did not know him and I don't know what he was. I know him as a General of the Croatian army, but I did not have any contact with General Bobetko at that time, and I don't know what he thought, neither did I talk to him about these documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at 406/10. You told us there were no ranks in the HVO. Let's look at that order by General Bobetko of the 20th of April, 1993. Sorry, 1992. I apologise. Tole's a Colonel, Siljeg is a Major, a couple of Captains. Four Captains, a Lieutenant, Major Lieutenants. Those are all ranks, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, you said yourself an hour ago that a decision was created on the 8th of April 1992 on the creation of the army. Your Honour, ranks are obtained on the basis of professional knowledge, and structure, and professional qualifications, and I don't think that any army in the world can, in 12 days, elaborate all the different ranks, mobilisation, development, and assign ranks to its members. Therefore, this order, I would say, was -- I maintain that the HVO did not have any ranks. It was only the commanders of the Operative Zones that had ranks and the chief of the main staff, but ranks as processes, as a form of command and control, was not instituted up until the Washington agreements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, were these HV ranks?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of these individuals, I know two. That is to say, I know the Colonel who in one month was promoted to Brigadier, and Zejko Siljeg who is mentioned here as Major. I don't know whether they are ranks referring to the Croatian army. I can read that it is Grude of the southern front, and I suppose that they could be ranks from the Croatian army, but I don't know that the HVO had a command of the southern front, that the HVO had its structures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, were these nine officers in the HV at the time of this order on the 20th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already said that I don't know their status. I know two of them with whom I had contacts. It is possible that they were officers of the Croatian army engaged in the IZM of Grude. I said that here in the order it says, "In order to have more effective command." As far as I can recall, this was operations at Kupres, and preventing the complete encirclement of Bosnia-Herzegovina by the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, who did you know in this list in addition to Tole? Who did you know?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I knew Colonel Zeljko Siljeg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, was either Siljeg or Tole in the HV at some time or at this time, either one?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that I don't know their status. Possibly they were. I cannot confirm that, because I never saw a document as to their status.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you know that at one time Zarko Tole was in the HV, don't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that he was, but I said that his status documents, that is to say, had he had some something from the Personnel Department of the Croatian army, a document to that effect, I never saw it and never discussed his status with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you talk to him about that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: About their status, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, about his service in the HV and the fact that he was with the 114 Brigade of the HV?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not discuss that fact with him, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you -- excuse me. Let me turn to a particular document. This is a new document, if I may, and it's a document prepared by the UN Civil Affairs in December of 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: If I may, just before you leave this document. General, would you look at the opening lines again, which you read? "In order to achieve effective operational and secure command in the units of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, the following are appointed." What was your impression from that, that these gentlemen are appointed to military positions in the HVO or that they're appointed to military positions in the HV and merely assigned to function in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your Honour, the title of the document is, "Appointment of officers to the defence command of Tomislavgrad." Tomislavgrad is a municipality south of the Kupres heights. It is a strategically important high ground for the defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. But I too find it unclear, because in the introduction that you read out, Your Honour, the commander wishes to achieve, "effective operational and secure command in the units of the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna," but they are not -- the HVO units did not exist only in Tomislavgrad. The order itself is slightly contradictory, and I believe it is the command of the HVO in Tomislavgrad which is oriented towards the Kupres battleground. Quite possibly at that time in that command there were also officers of the HV, but that is my belief because I did not actually see their documents. So I can only suppose that to be so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's not impossible. According to the knowledge you had of Mr. Tole and Mr. Zeljko Siljeg, it is not at all impossible that at least these two persons and, therefore, the others too could have been part of the Croatian army? It is not impossible?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Chairman, I said that it was possible that some of these officers were also officers of the HV, Croatian army. That's what I said. Perhaps there was a different interpretation. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you. No, I don't think there was any error in the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This is a document that has not been translated either into BCS or into French, but it is a document prepared by the UN Civil Affairs. If we can put -- and the bottom of the page is 00263649 on, which is the sixth page. That's the page.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is Exhibit number 579.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this particular document prepared by UN Civil Affairs, General, and the date of this document is the 10th of December, 1994, this reflects that Brigadier Zarko Tole is your chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Would you repeat the date, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date here is 10 December, 1994. That's the date of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can the witness see the document, please, Mr. President? He's being asked about a document in a foreign language, that he hasn't been shown and I think he should be shown the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I agree with Mr. Hayman. And more so as I didn't quite understand where this document comes from and I don't know what page we're talking about. Thank you for wanting to proceed quickly but, still, we have to know where we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a document, Mr. President, that is prepared by the United Nations Civil Affairs section, and six pages in, the number on the bottom should be 00263649. Six pages in is the page that's on the ELMO, or was on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: General Blaskic, did you find the relevant page of this document? Please continue, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, is the Zarko Tole that is named as your chief of staff the same Zarko Tole that we have been talking about in these exhibits that are signed by Janko Bobetko? Is that the same man?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Your question seems to imply something that is not correct. Mr. President, Your Honours, Brigadier General Zarko Tole was never the chief of staff while I was the chief of the main staff, and it is illogical -- just one moment, "Brigadier General," in Croatia, that is a rank that is two steps higher -- that he be subordinate to a Major General. I also wish to comment on this document further. I was never the commander of the main staff, as it is written in the document. I was the chief of the main staff of the HVO, and my deputy was Brigadier Major Miljenko Lasic on the 10th of December, '94. Nedjeljko Obradovic who is third on the list in this document, Your Honours, at that time was the commander of the military district of Mostar. In this document, there is something else that is incorrect, and that is, it is incorrect that the commander of the Operative Zone, if I'm reading it properly, of Northeast Herzegovina, Bozo Raguz, at that time, that Operative Zone did not exist. What existed was the Mostar military district, and the commander of that was Nedjeljko Obradovic. Furthermore, another thing is incorrect in this document, and that is that the commander of the Operative Zone of Northwest Herzegovina was Colonel Zeljko Siljeg. That operative zone did not exist either. What existed was the military district of Tomislavgrad, and the commander of that at that time was Brigadier Zeljko Glasnovic. Another thing is incorrect in the document, and that is that General Filip Filipovic, commander of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia, he was a commander of the Vitez military district rather, and General Dzuro Matuzovic was the commander of the military district of Bosanska Posavina. So to all events, Brigadier Zarko Tole was not in the main staff of the HVO when I was the chief of the main staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this document is wrong, that he was never your direct subordinate; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not referring to the document but to this page of that document, which says that Brigadier General Zarko Tole was the chief of staff or the chief of the main staff - I do not understand English so I'm not quite sure - but he was never chief of the main staff while I was the chief of the main staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was never your direct subordinate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He, as a person, was never my direct subordinate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. You have never had a discussion with him about his service in the HV; is that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I spoke to him in person on the 19th or, rather, the beginning of May - if necessary, I can check in my chronology - at a meeting in Busovaca. If it is important, I can repeat what we discussed in 1992, and after that, I had no further contact with him --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, sir.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- re any kind of conversations or discussions, and I was not his superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to two other photographs before we move to the other documents. These are two new documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 580 and 581. Exhibit 581 is the one showing three persons on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is 580 and this is 581. All right. We will go with 580 first.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going through these photographs, of course, you recognise the individuals in those photographs, sir?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who are they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: President Franjo Tudjman and the chief of the main staff of the Croatian army, General Janko Bobetko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us move to the next photograph, Prosecutor's Exhibit 581. Those three individuals from left to right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The late defence minister, Gojko Susak, President Franjo Tudjman, and the chief of the main staff of the Croatian army, General Janko Bobetko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With regard to Gojko Susak, he is the minister of defence for what country, sir?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was the minister of defence of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can move to another document, but before that, I would like to ask you a few questions about your subsequent meetings after Tole. You noted for us during your testimony that you met with an individual by the name of Zulu on 5 June, 1992; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us during your interview with Mr. Leach on the 12th of June, 1993, at page 00410998, that this individual's name was Zoric. I think the first name is Bruno. Do you now know the name of this individual whose nom de guerre you had as Zulu?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Which page were you referring to or rather when was that conversation with the gentleman?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The conversation with the gentleman was on the 12th of June, 1996. The page reference is 00410998, where you referred to a Bruno Zoric. Excuse me, 12th of June -- that's right, 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: While we're waiting, Mr. Usher, if you can just take this so we can move this along.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, maybe I can help you out and we can move this along. Was the individual you knew as Zulu's last name Zoric?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm not sure as to his identity, whether it's "Zoric" or "Zorica" or "Zorice." That is why I wanted to check because I am not sure of his identity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe we can help you out with the next exhibit, General. We may be able to move things along with the next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is Exhibit 582, 582A for the French version, and 582B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, reading this document again, this is an order signed by General Janko Bobetko on Republic of Croatia stationery, and it talks about dispatching the Frankopan battalion to Central Bosnia. It's very short and we'll just read it quickly, not too quickly for the interpreters. "In order to strengthen the defence of Bugojno and to secure and strengthen the Donji Vakuf-Bugojno line, I hereby order: 1. The Frankopan battalion shall be prepared and dispatched to Bugojno. 2. The Commander, Major Ivan Zoric -- "

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please go on to your question as soon as the witness has familiarised himself with this document because it is rather brief. There's no need to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This Major Ivan Zoric, Zulu, that is the individual who you met on the 5th of June, 1992 who described himself as the commander for Central Bosnia, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can answer what I told Mr. Leach during the interview. I know a man who introduced himself as Zulu on the 5th of June, 1992. I later learnt that his name was Bruno Zorica but somebody else told me that, that is, his deputy. His name was Bruno Zorica, and that is what is stated in my statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor. "Surname, Zorica," and first name, I think, was Bruno. I cannot confirm whether that is the same man under point 2, though the nickname is the same, "Zulu," but here it says, "Ivan Zoric."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, during your entire career in Bosnia, did you meet anybody else with the nom de guerre of "Zulu"?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that I met one man with the nom de guerre "Zulu." I remember him well. If you have a photograph, I could identify him on the photograph, but he introduced himself -- not he, but rather I learnt that his name was Bruno Zorica, "Zorica" being the surname and "Bruno" the first name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This individual that you met as "Zulu" on the 5th of June, 1992 introduced himself to you as the new commander in Central Bosnia, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct. That person, Zulu, introduced himself as the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone on the 5th of June, 1992. That is what I heard and saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Brigadier Zarko Tole that we see referenced in number 3 is the Brigadier Zarko Tole that we've been talking about throughout the afternoon, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It is the brigadier who, a month earlier, was a colonel assigned the task to form a command post in Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, this is signed by Janko Bobetko on Republic of Croatia letterhead.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. The aim of sending these forces is to strengthen the defence along the Donja Vakuf-Bugojno line. Donja Vakuf had been captured by the Serbs and the front line was in the immediate vicinity of the town of Bugojno.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many troops did General Bobetko have at his disposal that he was ordering around, both HVO and HV?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really do not know the answer to that question. I have already said that at the time I was commander of the armed units in Kiseljak municipality, and I was engaged in defence preparations for the Kiseljak municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
