utterances.text: Now, General, during the course of your testimony, in questions from my learned colleague, Mr. Nobilo, you noted, and I can pull the page references out for you, that you weren't getting any orders from Pasko Ljubicic, and you didn't get any orders from Zarko Tole, and then you didn't get any orders from Zulu; do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said that while I was in Kiseljak, I submitted my reports to the municipal staff of Kiseljak or, rather, the crisis staff there and that the control and command on the ground was not operational, in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not my question, General. Did you testify in response to questions from Mr. Nobilo that you weren't getting any orders after your meeting with Pasko Ljubicic, and you didn't get any orders after your meeting with Zarko Tole, and you didn't get any orders after your meeting with Zulu? Did you say that on direct examination?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not, as the commander of the armed units of Kiseljak - I must repeat once again my position - I did not receive orders from the persons you mention.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were you, by that testimony, attempting to lead this Chamber to believe that you weren't receiving orders from a command structure? Were you attempting to lead this Chamber to believe that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please rephrase your question better. I think that it is not easily understandable. Could you rephrase your question, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You noted that you didn't get any orders from your three --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Take your time. Be more precise as to what the witness said in the examination-in-chief and leave aside for the moment whether the Judges were led to believe this or that. It is up to them to make their own conclusions. Please try and rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, the reality is that when you were meeting with these three commanders, you were receiving written commands from a superior command structure; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You're referring to meetings with whom? Which meeting? Could you try and be more specific in time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Please give a specific date. I can understand General Blaskic. He needs to place this within a certain date. The accused certainly never said that he did not receive any superior orders, maybe in this time frame. Could you be specific about the date?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, from the time you took over, from the 23rd of April, 1992 through May, were you getting orders from a command structure superior to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Now it's clear.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From the 23rd of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the 23rd of April, when you took over as the head of the military and the municipal staff in Kiseljak, from the 23rd of April through May, were you getting orders from a superior command structure?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: From commanders from the command of the Operative Zone, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyone.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Anyone in the sense of certain organisational documents or administrative orders, there may have been some. I could look it up in the chronology, if necessary, but I was speaking about orders for the functioning of the system of control and command. I did not have any organised control and command system from any superiors. That is what I said. There may have been some administrative organisational documents, because these were the beginnings of the formation of the HVO. But the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone in the military and professional sense was not functioning, and I still stick to that assertion. That was the actual state of affairs. I just wish to underline that I was simultaneously engaged in organising defence and creating the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your testimony, you didn't receive any orders for the functioning of the system of control and command, and I'm reading the transcript that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Not quite. I understand, Mr. Kehoe. The witness has just made a statement as to what he did in that period when he took over command in Kiseljak. The Prosecutor is connecting this in relation to the statement he made before. I think the question is clear. General Blaskic, please answer that question.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already answered that the functioning of the control and command system did not exist. That was the situation in reality, but there may have been certain organisational orders regarding the establishment of the HVO because these were the beginnings of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but globally, if I understand you well, you're saying that you confirm that overall there was no command structure. I think that is the gist of the question.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Please. Fine. Please go on, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you a series of exhibits, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. President, so as not to interrupt later on, perhaps we could have a break now, because we have been working for more than 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Allow the President to be flexible with regard to the breaks. We are managing the time for the benefit of the witness but it is, after all, not acceptable, whenever there is a delicate question, that we should have a break. So allow us to go to the core of the question. Does this document have to do with the same point?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Let's at least show the witness the document and then we'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Judge, it's actually a series of documents. If we're not going to get through all those documents, I'd prefer not to start with one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: That's what we were suggesting, Mr. President. We weren't trying to interrupt counsel's flow. He said he had a number of documents to look at. It made sense, if we're going to have another break, to have it so that we didn't interrupt counsel's presentation. That was our only intent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I suggest that if we're going to go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Allow me to consult with my colleagues. (Trial Chamber deliberates)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a few minutes, please. (Private session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 1 (redacted) 2 (redacted) 3 (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Open session)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Mr. Prosecutor, let us look at your documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I just can get a time frame as to how long to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. You're quite right. We're going to go on until 5.30, in agreement with my colleagues. So we'll be working on the cross-examination for 20 minutes. Then we will adjourn the cross-examination. We will have a ten-minute break to allow the interpreters to have a rest and to organise the courtroom. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Then we will resume at 5.40, 5.45 for a brief ex parte meeting. Is that clear now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. If I could move to the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The ex parte will not be too long, Mr. Prosecutor? I'm thinking of the interpreters. Five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: That means ten? The interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We'll manage.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So is Exhibit 583 and 583A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, if you could take a look at this. This is an order that is written by the HVO president Mate Boban on the 10th of April, 1992. Before we go into this, General, this is the same individual that you met in Grude on the 27th of June, 1992; is it not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I met him then for the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you could review this particular document, General?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: As I don't have the French version, could you summarise it very briefly? It's a document concerning --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This is a document, Mr. President, that is dated the 10th of April, 1992, two days after the formation of the HVO, executed by the HVO president Mate Boban, and that it calls for or says that the Croatian Defence Council is the only -- well, it says, "This body is the only legal one and only this name is official." In the bottom paragraph it says, "All other military formations in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna are illegal or hostile."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. So you are placing the emphasis on the last part of the document; aren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you. Have you been able to look through it now, General Blaskic? Have you been able to look through it quickly?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, just a couple of more moments, because I'm reviewing it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But you have it in Serbo-Croatian, do you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Just one more minute perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had a chance to review that, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I have now, but I had never seen the document before. I see that the document was signed by president Mate Boban. Again, I did not talk to him regarding the authorship of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, this document does call for all military formations, other than the HVO, in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna are now illegal or hostile.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Hostile were probably the military formations of the Republika Srpska or the Territorial Defence as components of the JNA who, as you can see from the document, had already been attacking Ravno. This is as early as 1991. Then Kupres, Mostar, and so on. In April when, I arrived there, there were a number of military formations there, including armed peasants, criminal groups, and other military formations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the second to last paragraph, General, it does reflect, does it not, that the HVO has a main staff, that the HVO has municipal staffs in all the municipalities of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, and starting today, 10 April, 1992, the HVO main staff will communicate only with the municipal staffs of the HVO and that was, of course, the staff that you became a part of on the 14th of April; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. This is an order, and it is clear that the main staff was to be formed. It does say that the HVO has its main staff, but if the decision was taken on 8th of April, on 10 April I don't think that the factual state of affairs was such that all the main headquarters at the main staff and all the municipal staffs were already established. That did not correspond to what I have found on the ground, in the field. In fact, during that period I was arrested.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, General, based on this order by Mate Boban, you received orders from the main staff to implement those things that Boban calls for, i.e. declaring any other military formation illegal; did you not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: All military formations, as I pointed out, including armed criminal gangs and formations which were in existence in the areas of particular municipalities and which were not part of the system of command and control, but these were attempts at establishing the armed forces. However, the factual state on the ground was different. Unfortunately, these were just attempts. This order is two days later than the decision to establish the HVO. Who can establish the headquarters and all the formations within two days? I had never seen these documents before today, bearing the signature of Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, did you or did you not receive orders from the main staff to implement the order of Boban, i.e. to declare all other military formations illegal within the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna? Did you receive such orders from the main staff?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was receiving orders to that effect. I think that this was from the main staff, but let me repeat again. The factual state of affairs on the ground was that this was the beginning of the establishment of the HVO. So let me repeat. The HVO was established on the 8th of April, and on the 10th it claims that both the main staff and the municipal staffs are all operational. That is just within two days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you the next document, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Again, this is a new document, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 584, 584A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, this is an order that you received that's dated the 8th of May, 1992, signed by General Ante Roso. In this document, again it declares, in number 1, that all legal units -- "Only legal military units of the HVO. All other military units must join the HVO and recognise the HVO main staff as their supreme command." In number 5, "This order supersedes all orders of the Territorial Defence command which will be considered illegal in this territory." Now, you received this order, did you not, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I received this order, but at the time, the only legal force defending Bosnia was the JNA. This was the 8th of May, 1992. And a component of these armed forces was the Territorial Defence, so this same Yugoslav People's Army, whose component was the Territorial Defence which was attacking Bosnia-Herzegovina, was, according to the constitution or whatever else, was the only legal armed force in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on this order coming from General Ante Roso, you issued orders, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of this order, I had an obligation to issue this type of order for the area where I was the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take a look at two of those orders, General, first starting with Defence Exhibit 199. This is a Defence Exhibit, General, so I assume you've read it before, and in the prefatory paragraph, you note two orders coming from the main staff, and that order that you reference coming from the main staff is 01-331/92, and that's the order of General Roso that was two days before.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I referred to those orders. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At this particular juncture, by Defence Exhibit 199, the order that we looked at coming from Boban has been passed down to the HVO main staff, and the HVO main staff in the name of General Ante Roso has issued an order to the municipalities, and you have implemented that order?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know who received the order from Mate Boban that you're referring to and whether it was Ante Roso that did so, but in this order, I referred to the order from the main staff, and I provided the reference number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Ante Roso's order from the main staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. The chief of the main staff was Brigadier Milivoj Petkovic. In the document which you are referring to, which is Defence Exhibit 199, it does not state that Ante Roso was the chief of the main staff, and as far as I know, he was not chief of the main staff of the HVO at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at this prior order from Ante Roso, and what, in fact, is the number on that document?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I recognise the 01 -- I can read it but I can't read the next one. Is it "93"? This is "331" or "931"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 01-331, and what you have listed in your prefatory paragraph is 01-331 also, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, an objection to the fact that the registration number is 01-331/92. It is hardly legible, and in my opinion, it could very well be 01-931/92.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, the document speaks for itself, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would agree with me, General, that the content of this document, this order coming from General Roso, is an item that's reflected in Defence Exhibit 199; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, no objection to the question whether he remembers what the prior order was, but the order -- it is the same number, I think, but it's a different date. This order is dated the 8th, and in the order which is Exhibit D199, the order of that number is dated as having been the 10th of April, two days later. So if he remembers, fine, but the documents, there's some lack of clarity in the documents, and he shouldn't have to say, "Yes. The documents integrate in a certain way or they don't." The documents are what they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We will clarify the date by moving to the next document which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Objection sustained. It is a fact that the order D580 alludes to the date of the 10th of April, refers to the date of the 10th of April. The 8th of May has another number. Something is not clear there, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, and I think that we can clarify it by looking at Prosecution Exhibit 502 where the same number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think we will leave the clarification of this matter for tomorrow morning. You wish to clarify it straightaway?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I could clarify this quickly, yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very quickly, please. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have Exhibit 502 before you, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have it now?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Read the top paragraph of Exhibit 502.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: "On the basis of the orders received from the main staff, confidential number 01-" and then crossed out "331/92," it says "of 8 or 9 May, 1992 and with the intention of defining precisely the legal status of all formations, I issue the following order." This is the document dated 11 May, 1992. Should I read the rest of the order?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not at this point, General. But you would agree with me that the date is 8 May, 1992 and reflects the number 01-331/92, which is the same number and the same date as Roso has on his order; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The "3" has been crossed out. I don't know why. It says, "01-3," and then the next digit 3 is crossed out, at least in my copy, and then "1/92."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Absent the crossing out of that particular 3, is that the same number and is that the same date?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but can I just review the contents of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The mistake, if any, in 502, Mr. President, is on the translation in the English version that has got the date wrong. The date is correct in the original BCS version. With that, Mr. President, I will go into the content of these documents in greater length tomorrow, unless Your Honours want to proceed. I'm at the Court's disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think that we are going to adjourn. Will you take these documents, Mr. Registrar? Let us have about ten minutes. Will that be sufficient, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. The hearing is adjourned as concerns the cross-examination of the witness, and we will resume in another format in about ten minutes.
